_note: Figure LOD (docs/PLAN_LOD_DRAW_DISTANCE.md step D, src/game/figlod.ts). A battle royale's bots cost more than its map: each figure is about 13.7k triangles on 65 bones with its own materials, its gun another 11 to 15 meshes, and every one of them animates and casts a shadow every frame however far away it is. So: the animation runs every frame within `near` metres of the camera, every second frame out to `mid`, every fourth beyond that, and not at all off screen past `offscreen` metres (the mixer is given the time it missed when its turn comes, so nothing drifts). A figure casts a shadow only within `shadow` metres. Past `farGun` metres its gun is the one merged mesh the floor guns use (loot.ts), not the 11 to 15 of the full model. The distances are ours, judged by what a figure is worth on screen at each: at 30 m a figure is a target, at 80 m a shape, beyond that a dot. Nothing here changes what a bullet hits: hit boxes come from the figure's own boxes, not from the animation. A soldier's eyes are a mesh and a draw call of their own (apex-lobby counted bots at about 125 of 540 draw calls in a Neon street frame, 2026-10-04): they never cast a shadow, and past `eyes` metres they are not drawn. The head is open behind them (photographed: hidden, the sockets show what is behind the head), so not at 25 m, where the opening is still 0.8 of a pixel at 1080p and could twinkle against a bright sky, but at 60, a third of a pixel, where a figure already casts no shadow.
_zoom: Milestone 846: the bands weigh a figure's size on screen, and an aimed view makes it bigger, so an enemy on screen is judged at its distance over the zoom from the hip's view (figlod.ts seen). At 100 m through a 4x scope it looks 25 m off and animates every frame, with its eyes, where it played at 15 poses a second, its gun the merged mesh: at x8 it looked like a near soldier in stop motion. A figure off screen keeps its real distance, so an aim costs only the figures it shows, and a narrow view shows few. Its shadow comes with it (Milestone 848; 846 kept it on the real distance, on the mistaken belief that the sun's map did not reach): the sun's shadow map covers the whole of the place (range.ts setShadowRegion, 230 m each way over the battle royale's map), so a scoped figure past 60 m stood with no shadow where every wall beside it had one.
_rates: Milestone 626: a band's stride is counted in frames, so on a fast machine a figure out of the near band animated far more often than it needs to (170 fps gave a mid figure 85 poses a second and a far one 42, where 60 fps gives them 30 and 15). Past `near` a figure is held to `midHz` (to `mid` metres) or `farHz` (beyond) poses a second at any frame rate, and never fewer frames apart than its band's stride: what 60 fps always looked like. Within `near` a figure still animates every frame, as a fight up close needs. ?slow=lodhz puts the old strides back for measuring.
